svg.title: Each normal form removes one named anomaly
svg.desc: One wide table repeating the same customer and city on three order rows, with the city column ringed in red and one value misspelled to show the update anomaly. Three numbered steps below name what each normal form removes, and the result is drawn as three tables — customers, orders and order_items — linked by hand-drawn foreign key arrows, beside a green box showing a deliberate denormalization and its write cost.
svg.text: Each normal form removes one named anomaly
one wide table: the same fact stored three times
one typo and the data now
1NF - no repeating groups: one sku per row
2NF - no partial dependency on part of a composite key
3NF - no transitive deps: city depends on the CUSTOMER
anomaly. Say which one, or you are
each fact stored exactly once · the planner then eliminated the customers join entirely: 0.060 ms
denormalize on purpose: copy city onto orders
the cost: every write must now update both
...and what does the PLANNER do with these keys?
